query: The Co-free FeNiCrMn system was selected to reduce cost while retaining the mechanical performance of equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi; prior work reported comparable or better mechanical properties after excluding Co. Research on FeNiCrMn has mainly addressed corrosion, while studies of related high- and medium-entropy alloys examined dynamic responses under tension or compression, different temperatures and strain rates, compositional changes, and the presence of cracks or voids. Those studies established that dynamic properties are sensitive to loading regime and material condition, but their different chemistries and defect states do not identify what governs FeNiCrMn. Under the constraints of retaining the Co-free composition and its strength–ductility balance, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis explains the dynamic behavior of solidified FeNiCrMn across temperature and strain-rate regimes? Define a controlled study capable of testing the hypothesis, its applicable boundaries, the prior findings that support it, and a result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: The dynamic behavior of solidified FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy is governed by a thermally activated dislocation glide mechanism, which is sensitive to temperature and strain rate.
generation.material_initial_state: Solidified FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy with a Co-free composition
generation.intervention: Systematic variation of temperature (from -196°C to 500°C) and strain rate (from 10^-3 s^-1 to 10^3 s^-1)
generation.conditions: Uniaxial tensile loading, with a constant strain rate and temperature
generation.mechanism: Thermally activated dislocation glide, influenced by the interaction between dislocations and solute atoms
generation.predicted_outcome: A 20% increase in yield strength and a 30% decrease in ductility at high strain rates (above 10^2 s^-1) and low temperatures (below 0°C), relative to the baseline (room temperature and a strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1)
generation.baseline: Room temperature (20°C) and a strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1
generation.boundary: Temperature range: -196°C to 500°C, strain rate range: 10^-3 s^-1 to 10^3 s^-1
generation.uncertainty: The exact relationship between dislocation density, mobility, and the dynamic behavior of FeNiCrMn is not well understood, and the role of solute atoms in influencing dislocation glide is still unclear.

falsification_experiment.design: Uniaxial tensile testing with in-situ temperature and strain rate control
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the yield strength and ductility of FeNiCrMn do not vary by more than 10% with temperature and strain rate, the hypothesis is falsified.
